clues.title: Coverage: Low cam
text: All the coverage taken in Japan is low-cam, the only two other countries with low-cam is Sri Lanka and Switzerland but they look different. You can recognize lowcam because of wide blur of the street view car and lower vantage point compared to normal camera.

text: **Japan has three common variations of road lines. They are as follows:**
The most common being white, solid outer lines with a dashed white middle line.
White solid sidelines with a yellow solid middle line.
White solid sidelines with yellow and white middle lines.

clues.title: Lowcam
text: **Due to privacy reasons, the camera is intentionally set lower to the ground.**
**This is known as low-cam.**
**You can identify it by:**
Looking downwards.
The blur will be noticeably larger.
The road will look wider, and objects will be viewed from a lower perspective.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Architecture: North & South - Roof Transition
text: The further you are north, roofs generally transition from tiled to level or flat sloped in order to compensate for heavy snowfall.
Northern houses often have ladders attached to the side, giving roof access to clear snow.
In addition to north to south, high-elevation mountainous regions or high snowfall areas often use such roofs, even in more central or southern prefectures.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Bollard: Tohoku Bollard
text: This **thick**, white bollard, found in the Tohoku region, will have an **octagonal reflector**, and **yellow stripe** just underneath. In addition, you can find the same bollard, but with a rectangular top.

Finally, there are two other variations. You can find a **black octagonal**, and **rectangular** version. They are often found on National Highways or Expressways and can have the number printed on them.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Bollard: Striped Bollard
text: These striped bollards (which cover over the original) have a **thinner top half**, and **no reflectors**, and are common to the Tohoku region. They are especially common in Akita prefecture.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Bollard: Akita Bollard
text: This bollard, much like Tohoku, will be a **thick**, white bollard with an **octagonal reflector**. However, this Akita prefecture variation will have **two yellow stripes** underneath the reflector.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Bollard: Aomori Bollard
text: This bollard, found in the Aomori prefecture, has **two yellow stripes**, a single circular reflector, and is **extendable**. Sometimes, only one thicker stripe near the top may be present.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Bollard: Toyama Bollard
text: The Toyama prefecture bollard has **one reflector**, is **extendable** and has a **red stripe** underneath the reflector.
**NOTE:** Be careful: if there is either a second reflector, or a yellow stripe instead of a red one, these are different bollards. These are more common variations found across many prefectures.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Bollard: Kyushu/Yamaguchi Bollard
text: This flat, white bollard, found on the island of Kyushu and in Yamaguchi Prefecture, will have a **series of separated orange reflectors** on one side, and the same **white** on the opposite.
**NOTE:** Rarely, you may find similar bollards in Hokkaido. However, both sides will have orange reflectors.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Bollard: Okayama Bollard

clues.title: Pole: Infrastructure - Poletop Extension - Angled

clues.title: Pole: Infrastructure - Transformer - Two Bars
text: The electrical poles in Hokkaido either have this plus-shaped bar attached to the side of the pole, or one transformer mounted on two bars. The Kanto Transformer may also be mounted on two bars.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Infrastructure - Transformer - Two on Square
text: In Hokkaido, if there is more than one transformer, they will often be mounted on the sides of a square.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Plate: Infrastructure - Transformer - Round Plate / Zigzag Bar
text: The transformers in Tohoku, which often have additional square holding brackets and the logo of the Tohoku Electrical Company, are sometimes mounted on a round plate with a zigzag bar.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Infrastructure - Transformer - One on Square
text: In Tohoku, you may also find transformers mounted on the side of a square, with a straight bar mounted on the top of the square. Rarely, you may find a square without a bar.
NOTE: While Kansai may have a square attachment as well, the bar will be mounted on the bottom rather than the top.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Plate: Infrastructure - Transformer - 2 or 3 Insulators
text: The transformers in Kanto, which can have three or two insulators, are often mounted on a wooden plate and two bars, or a round plate and a T-shaped bar.
NOTE: While the Hokkaido transformer may also be mounted on two bars, it will never have a wooden plate. Kanto ones can also be mounted without a wooden plate.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Plate: Infrastructure - Transformer - Wooden Plate
text: The transformers in Kanto, which can have three or two insulators, are often mounted on a wooden plate and two bars, or a round plate and a T-shaped bar.
NOTE: While the Hokkaido transformer may also be mounted on two bars, it will never have a wooden plate. Kanto ones can also be mounted without a wooden plate.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Plate: Infrastructure - Transformer - Round Plate / T-Bar
text: The transformers in Kanto, which can have three or two insulators, are often mounted on a wooden plate and two bars, or a round plate and a T-shaped bar.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Infrastructure - Transformer - Lamp-Shaped Insulator
text: The transformers in Hokuriku, which are attached with thin metal bars, often have these small “lamp” shaped insulators. There will never be a bar present except for the attachment mentioned above.
NOTE: The prefecture of Niigata will have the Tohoku transformer design, as opposed to Hokuriku one.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Infrastructure - Transformer - Triangle
text: The transformers in Chubu, which often have painted yellow numbers and black “tap” connectors, are either attached with large triangle and horizontal bars, or these thin metal brackets.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Infrastructure - Transformer - Black Tap Connector

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Infrastructure - Transformer - Square / Bottom Bar
text: The transformers in Kansai have either a straight or zigzag bar mounted on the bottom of a square. The transformer(s) will be mounted on the sides of that same square.
While this is uncommon, the bar and transformer(s) may be mounted on a vertical bar, rather than a square.
NOTE: While Tohoku may have a square attachment as well, the bar will be mounted on the top rather than the bottom

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Pole: Infrastructure - Transformer - Cross (Chugoku Variant)
text: The transformers in Chugoku, which have a cross-shaped bar attached in the middle of the pole, mounted by a full triangle, will have a long horizontal or short vertical insulator(s) at the end.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Infrastructure - Transformer - Red Number
text: In Chugoku, a white sticker will often be stuck to the bottom of the transformer with red numbers. They may also be painted on the side.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Pole: Infrastructure - Transformer - Cross (Hat Insulator)

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Infrastructure - Transformer - White Sticker

clues.title: Pole: Infrastructure - Transformer - Kyushu

clues.title: Pole: Infrastructure - Transformer - Okinawa

clues.title: Bollard: Infrastructure - Bollard - Orange Reflector
text: This flat, white bollard, found on the island of Kyushu and in Yamaguchi Prefecture, will have a series of separated orange reflectors on one side, and the same white on the opposite.
NOTE: Rarely, you may find similar bollards in Hokkaido. However, both sides will have orange reflectors.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Bollard: Infrastructure - Bollard - Black Stripe
text: Some bollards on the island of Shikoku can have a black stripe just under the reflector. They can be found normally, attached to guardrails or walls.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Bollard: Infrastructure - Bollard - Tohoku
text: This thick, white bollard, found in the Tohoku region, will have an octagonal reflector, and yellow stripe just underneath. In addition, you can find the same bollard, but with a rectangular top.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Bollard: Infrastructure - Bollard - Tohoku (Black Variant)
text: Additionally to regular Tohoku bollards, there are two other variations. You can find a black octagonal, and rectangular version. They are often found on National Highways or Expressways and can have the number printed on them.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Bollard: Infrastructure - Bollard - Akita
text: This bollard, much like Tohoku, will be a thick, white bollard with an octagonal reflector. However, this Akita prefecture variation will have two yellow stripes underneath the reflector.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Bollard: Infrastructure - Bollard - Toyama
text: The Toyama prefecture bollard has one reflector, is extendable and has a red stripe underneath the reflector.
NOTE: Be careful: if there is either a second reflector, or a yellow stripe instead of a red one, these are different bollards. These are more common variations found across many prefectures.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Bollard: Infrastructure - Bollard - Okoyama
text: This bollard, with an octagonal reflector, and red stripe underneath it, is exclusive to the Okayama prefecture. Additionally, there will be a sloped connection where the base meets the reflector.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Bollard: Infrastructure - Bollard - Aomori
text: This bollard, found in the Aomori prefecture, has two yellow stripes, a single circular reflector, and is extendable. Sometimes, only one thicker stripe near the top may be present.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Bollard: Infrastructure - Bollard - Striped / No Reflector
text: These striped bollards (which cover over the original) have a thinner top half, and no reflectors, and are common to the Tohoku region. They are especially common in Akita prefecture.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Bollard: Infrastructure - Bollard - Extendable
text: In the northern parts of the Chugoku region, you can primarily find these basic snow poles, with either a thin extended, or thin contracted top. They can also sometimes be found in Iwate.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Guardrail: Infrastructure - Guardrail - Green Band
text: Green bands on guardrails are most commonly found in Oita and Miyazaki, but can be found on all of Kyushu.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Guardrail: Infrastructure - Guardrail - Hokkaido Sticker
text: You can find these chevron-like stickers, or more rarely orange ones, on guardrails in Hokkaido.
On the end or side of a guardrail.
Stuck to metal posts between wire fences, which are often found in Hokkaido.
On railings, which are often found on bridges, underneath the inside of the railing.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Guardrail: Infrastructure - Guardrail - Red-Yellow Stripes
text: Guardrail endings with these red and yellow striped stickers can commonly be found across Chugoku, except in Yamaguchi. They can also rarely be found in Niigata.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Infrastructure - Vertical Traffic Light
text: Vertical traffic lights can be found in Hokkaido, and along the northwestern coast. The usual horizontal traffic lights can be found everywhere else.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Sign: Infrastructure - Yellow Circle Sign
text: These specific black signs with two yellow circles are found in Kagawa. Other variations can be seen, including them stacked on top of each other, or with an arrow attached above.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Infrastructure - Claymore
text: Kerosine tanks, otherwise known as “Claymores”, can be found more commonly the further north you go. They are abundant in Hokkaido, but can be found in prefectures south of it, or in high elevation mountainous areas.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Infrastructure - Gas Tank
text: Hot water, gas and propane tanks can be found more frequently in northern prefectures or high elevation mountainous areas. Here are a few common variations you can find:
The standard hot water tank.
Covered propane tanks.
Exposed propane tanks.
These cylindrical tanks.
And finally, these circular tripod tanks.
Moreover, these are even more common in rural towns or villages, where major water or gas lines are unavailable.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Infrastructure - Shosetsu
text: Snow prevention roads, known as ‘Shosetsu’, are found mainly in northwest coastal prefectures. They appear as tiny circles in the pavement, and spray warm underground water to clear snow.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Infrastructure - Ehime Cycling Route
text: Cycling routes in Ehime use an outside white, with an inside blue line. They are more commonly found along the coast but may be found further inland too.
While exceptions do exist, and can be found in other prefectures, they are the extreme minority.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Vegetation: Vegetation - Bamboo
text: In general, bamboo grows more often in the south, and slowly decreases further north. Population size and areas where it grows can vary, so use this information primarily in helping assist your region guess.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Architecture: Architecture - Red Tiled Roof
text: These unique red-tiled roofs are most commonly found in Chugoku, especially in the prefectures of Hiroshima and Shimane.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Architecture: Architecture - Northern Roofs
text: The further you are north, roofs generally transition from tiled to level or flat sloped in order to compensate for heavy snowfall. Northern houses often have ladders attached to the side, giving roof access to clear snow.
NOTE: In addition to north to south, high-elevation mountainous regions or high snowfall areas often use such roofs, even in more central or southern prefectures.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Architecture: Architecture - Okinawa House
text: Okinawa can often be recognised by the white concrete buildings with flat roofs.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Vegetation: Vegetation - Giant Butterbur
text: Giant butterbur (commonly referred to as cabbage) is abundant in Hokkaido and some northern prefectures. Plants found south of Hokkaido often have smaller leaves. It is often found growing along the roadside.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Pole: Agriculture - Tea
text: Green tea plants are often grown in hedged rows. You will often see these fans mounted on poles, which serve the purpose of preventing frost from falling on the plants.
The prefectures of Shizuoka (36%) and Kagoshima (34%) make up the majority of the production, with Mie (7%), Miyazaki (4%), and other prefectures (17%) making up the minority.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Agriculture - Rice
text: Rice is mainly produced north of Tokyo. During growth, it resembles straws of grass. And when ready for harvest, brown husks are visible. They are also commonly planted in beds of water.
The regions of Chubu (21%), Kanto (15%), Tohoku (27%), and Hokkaido (7%) make up the majority of production.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Vegetation: Vegetation - Japanese White Birch
text: Japanese White Birch grows dominantly in the Chubu and Hokkaido regions, and to a lesser extent in Tohoku. Small areas of white birch can be found throughout Japan, so use this information primarily to help assist your region guess.
NOTE: Japanese Beech is another species of tree found in Japan. They, however, have more grey and spotted bark, as opposed to the mostly white Japanese White Birch.

clues.title: Vegetation: Vegetation - Chinese Silver Grass
text: Chinese Silver Grass, referred to as Kyushu grass, is indeed very abundant on the island of Kyushu. However, use this tip with caution, as they can be seen outside of this area.

NOTE: Another notable region they can be found in is the prefectures of Niigata, Yamagata and Akita. Though, combining the rather large quantity found on Kyushu, its normally distinct vegetation, along with other information, there often will be a clear distinction.

clues.title: Agriculture - Sugarcane
text: Sugarcane is almost exclusively found on the islands in southern Kyushu and Okinawa.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Coverage: Coverage Meta - Hokkaido Winter
text: Hokkaido has very limited winter and snow coverage. Unless you are certain, it is often better not to guess this prefecture. Though, if you do find yourself in Hokkaido, these regions are most likely. Other low amounts of miscellaneous coverage is primarily in the southern half of the island.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Landscape - Plains
text: Japan is notably a very mountainous country. However, there are some regions that are quite flat, being the Nobi and Kanto plains. While at times they can look very similar, determining that it is one or the other can be very helpful.
NOTE: While there are, of course, other flat areas in Japan, these two are the most recognizable.

clues.title: Architecture: Architecture - Shisa
text: You can find these ‘Shisa’ guardian lions and house plaques with these specific characters in Okinawa. The colour and shapes of both can vary.

clues.title: Landscape: Agriculture - Red Fields
text: Agricultural fields with red soil are commonly found on several southern islands, most notably on the islands of Miyakojima and Ishigaki in southern Okinawa.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Landscape - Mount Fuji
text: Mount Fuji is the tallest mountain in Japan, with a gradual incline and often snowy summit.
Depending on the elevation, it can be seen from far away. This can create some excellent region guesses, especially if you account for direction and distance.
